title: Bayer Strikes Up to USD3.25 Billion Cancer Drug Licensing Deal with China's Hansoh Pharma

contentHtml:
Bengaluru: China's Hansoh Pharmaceutical said on Wednesday three of its units had granted a unit of German drugmaker Bayer AG an exclusive license to its experimental cancer drug in a deal potentially worth up to USD 3.25 billion.

The license will allow Bayer Consumer Care AG to develop, manufacture and commercialize HS-20122 on a global scale, excluding mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan.

The Chinese drugmaker said its units, Hansoh (Shanghai) Healthtech, Shanghai Hansoh Biomedical and Changzhou Hansoh Pharmaceutical, will receive $150 million upfrontThe units will also be eligible for up to $3.1 billion in development, regulatory and sales milestones, plus tiered royalties on future net sales, according to the agreement.

HS-20122 is an experimental antibody-drug conjugate designed to target solid tumors by delivering cancer-killing therapy directly to tumour cells.Drugmakers around the world have struck more than a dozen licensing deals with Chinese biotech firms this year.

These include Anglo-Swedish drugmaker AstraZeneca's $18.5 billion obesity drug deal with CSPC Pharmaceutical in January and Bristol Myers Squibb's $15.2 billion deal with Jiangsu Hengrui in May.

Source : Reuters
